skills.name: Density: definition, calculation, units; density of a liquid

note.text:
Density is mass per unit volume: ρ = m ÷ V.
• Units: kg/m³ (SI) or g/cm³. 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³. Water: 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³.
• Rearranged: m = ρV and V = m ÷ ρ.
• A solid floats in a liquid if its density is less than that of the liquid.
Density of a liquid: measure a volume in a measuring cylinder, find its mass by difference on a balance, then divide.

sections.heading: Heavy for its size
sections.text:
A small iron nail sinks but a large log floats. The log has more mass, but it is less dense: each cubic centimetre of wood has less mass than a cubic centimetre of iron.
Density is mass per unit volume: ρ = m ÷ V (ρ is the Greek letter rho).

sections.heading: Units and rearranging
sections.text:
Units: g/cm³ or, in SI, kg/m³. Since {1} g/cm³ = {1000} kg/m³, water has density {1} g/cm³ = {1000} kg/m³.
• m = ρV: {200} cm³ of oil of density {0.9} g/cm³ has a mass of {180} g.
• V = m ÷ ρ.
Typical densities (g/cm³): cork {0.25}, wood {0.6}, palm oil {0.9}, water {1}, aluminium {2.7}, iron {7.9}, mercury {13.6}.

sections.heading: Density of a liquid
sections.text:
• Find the mass of an empty measuring cylinder.
• Pour in some liquid and read its volume.
• Find the new mass; subtract to get the mass of the liquid.
• Divide: ρ = m ÷ V.
Objects float in a liquid if they are less dense than it: that is why oil floats on water.

key_words.meaning: mass per unit volume, ρ = m ÷ V
stay on the surface: less dense than the liquid

mistake.why: Density is mass per unit volume: mass on top, volume underneath.

worked_example.problem: A block of aluminium has a mass of {m} g and a volume of {V} cm³. Find its density in g/cm³ and in kg/m³.
steps: {1} g/cm³ = {1000} kg/m³, so ρ = {m / V * 1000} kg/m³.

check.prompt: Convert a density of {r} g/cm³ to kg/m³.

misconceptions.explain: kg/m³ numbers are larger: multiply by {1000}.

questions.prompt: A stone has mass {m} g and volume {V} cm³. Find its density (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: Density is mass ÷ volume, not volume ÷ mass.

questions.prompt: Cooking oil has a density of {r} g/cm³. Find the mass of {V} cm³ of it (g).
Convert a density of {r} g/cm³ to kg/m³.

misconceptions.explain: kg/m³ numbers are larger: multiply by {1000}.

questions.prompt: An empty measuring cylinder has mass {e} g. With {V} cm³ of a liquid it has mass {e + m} g. Find the density of the liquid (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the empty cylinder first: only the liquid's mass counts.

questions.prompt: A solid has mass {m} g and volume {V} cm³. Will it float or sink in water (density {1} g/cm³)?
questions.correct: {m / V < 1 ? 'Float: its density is ' + fmt(density(m, V)) + ' g/cm³, less than water' : 'Sink: its density is ' + fmt(density(m, V)) + ' g/cm³, more than water'}

distractors.text: {m / V < 1 ? 'Sink: its density is ' + fmt(density(m, V)) + ' g/cm³, more than water' : 'Float: its density is ' + fmt(density(m, V)) + ' g/cm³, less than water'}
{m > 100 ? 'Sink: it is heavy' : 'Float: it is light'}

misconceptions.explain: Compare carefully: {density(m, V)} is {m / V < 1 ? 'less' : 'more'} than {1}.
Floating depends on density, not on mass alone: a heavy log of wood floats.
A solid denser than water (like a stone) sinks.
